To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the firing pattern of vasoconstricting preganglionic neurons in vivo is highly cardiac rhythmic; 2) most vasoconstrictive ganglion cells fire action potentials in vivo only when they are driven by a single preganglionic input, and 3) the threshold for action potential firing is set by the sum of the excitatory postsynaptically potentials generated by preganglionic inputs.

the majority of action potentials fired by sympathetic ganglion cells in the third thoracic sympathetic ganglion in vivo are triggered by single preganglionic synaptic inputs and that the majority of these preganglionic inputs are active only occasionally.

(1) in the third lumbral sympathetic ganglion of the rat, (2) most vasoconstrictors (3) are driven by (4) a few preganglionic neurons that (5) fire at low frequency (6) and (7) are highly barosensitive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the brain controls the cardiovascular system.
the function of the sympathetic ganglia in the rat.
how the sympathetic ganglion cell integrates synaptic inputs to generate the action potentials that control sympathetic outflow.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ganglion cell is not the relay, but the switch.
the vasoconstrictors of the rat are not simple relays, but are continuously variable gates.
ganglionic transmission in a vasoconstrictive vasomotor pathway is highly variable, but not random.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the sympathetic nervous system is organized in such a way that it can respond rapidly to changes in arterial blood pressure and that this response is not limited to the number of preganglionic neurons innervating a target organ.

the ganglion cell's firing pattern is a function of both the pattern of preganglionic input and of the cell's excitability, which is itself a function of its intrinsic membrane properties and of the pattern of preganglionically driven inputs.
the ganglion cell is a ‘variable’ rather than a ‘switch’.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sympathetic nervous system is a complex network that can be modulated in many ways.
the baroreflex is a dynamic process, not a simple switch.
the vasoconstrictors are more complex than previously thought.
